# google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster

A Vertex AI ModelDevelopmentCluster resource that manages a cluster of compute
resources with an orchestrator (such as Slurm or GKE) for model development
and training workloads.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

To get more information about ModelDevelopmentCluster, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations.modelDevelopmentClusters)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs)

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Model Development Cluster Basic


```hcl
data "google_project" "project" {
  provider = google-beta
}

resource "google_compute_network" "net" {
  provider                = google-beta
  name                    = "mdc-net"
  auto_create_subnetworks = false
}

resource "google_compute_subnetwork" "subnet" {
  provider                 = google-beta
  name                     = "mdc-subnet"
  ip_cidr_range            = "10.0.0.0/24"
  region                   = "us-central1"
  network                  = google_compute_network.net.id
  private_ip_google_access = true
}

resource "google_compute_firewall" "internal" {
  provider      = google-beta
  name          = "mdc-fw"
  network       = google_compute_network.net.name
  direction     = "INGRESS"
  source_ranges = ["10.0.0.0/24"]

  allow {
    protocol = "tcp"
    ports    = ["0-65535"]
  }
  allow {
    protocol = "udp"
    ports    = ["0-65535"]
  }
  allow {
    protocol = "icmp"
  }
}

resource "google_filestore_instance" "home" {
  provider = google-beta
  name     = "mdc-home"
  location = "us-central1-b"
  tier     = "BASIC_HDD"

  file_shares {
    capacity_gb = 1024
    name        = "share1"
  }

  networks {
    network = google_compute_network.net.name
    modes   = ["MODE_IPV4"]
  }
}

resource "google_filestore_instance" "data" {
  provider = google-beta
  name     = "mdc-data"
  location = "us-central1-b"
  tier     = "BASIC_HDD"

  file_shares {
    capacity_gb = 1024
    name        = "share1"
  }

  networks {
    network = google_compute_network.net.name
    modes   = ["MODE_IPV4"]
  }
}

resource "google_compute_reservation" "res" {
  provider                      = google-beta
  name                          = "mdc-res"
  zone                          = "us-central1-b"
  specific_reservation_required = true

  specific_reservation {
    count = 1
    instance_properties {
      machine_type = "n2-standard-4"
    }
  }
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster" "default" {
  provider                     = google-beta
  region                       = "us-central1"
  model_development_cluster_id = "tftest"
  display_name                 = "tftest"
  deletion_policy              = "DELETE"
  depends_on                   = [google_compute_firewall.internal]

  labels = {
    env = "dev"
  }

  runtime_spec {
    service_account = "${data.google_project.project.number}-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com"
  }

  lustre_export_config {
    destination_bucket = "mdc-backup-bucket"
    days_of_week       = ["MONDAY", "THURSDAY"]

    start_time {
      hours   = 4
      minutes = 30
    }
  }

  network {
    network    = google_compute_network.net.id
    subnetwork = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet.id
  }

  orchestrator_spec {
    slurm_spec {
      home_directory_storage = google_filestore_instance.home.id
      login_node_pool_id     = "login"
      default_partition_id   = "main"
      prolog_bash_scripts    = ["#!/bin/bash\necho prolog"]
      epilog_bash_scripts    = ["#!/bin/bash\necho epilog"]

      config = {
        PriorityType      = "priority/multifactor"
        PriorityWeightAge = "1000"
      }

      node_sets {
        node_pool_id = "compute"
        config = {
          Weight = "10"
        }
      }

      partitions {
        id            = "main"
        node_pool_ids = ["compute", "flexpool", "respool"]
        config = {
          PriorityTier = "10"
        }
      }
    }
  }

  node_pools {
    id                 = "compute"
    zone               = "us-central1-b"
    provisioning_model = "ON_DEMAND"
    node_image         = "projects/clusterdirector-public-images/global/images/family/common-ubuntu-2204-amd64-nvidia-580-slurm-2505-v20251113"
    startup_script     = "#!/bin/bash\necho hello"
    enable_public_ips  = true
    filestores         = [google_filestore_instance.data.id]

    labels = {
      pool = "compute"
    }

    boot_disk {
      boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
    }

    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n2-standard-4"
    }

    scaling_spec {
      min_node_count = 1
      max_node_count = 2
    }
  }

  node_pools {
    id                      = "flexpool"
    zone                    = "us-central1-b"
    provisioning_model      = "FLEX_START"
    flex_start_max_duration = "3600s"
    node_image              = "projects/clusterdirector-public-images/global/images/family/common-ubuntu-2204-amd64-nvidia-580-slurm-2505-v20251113"
    startup_script          = "#!/bin/bash\necho hello"
    enable_public_ips       = true
    filestores              = [google_filestore_instance.data.id]

    labels = {
      pool = "flexpool"
    }

    boot_disk {
      boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      boot_disk_type    = "hyperdisk-balanced"
    }

    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "a3-ultragpu-8g"
    }

    scaling_spec {
      min_node_count = 0
      max_node_count = 1
    }
  }

  node_pools {
    id                 = "login"
    zone               = "us-central1-b"
    provisioning_model = "ON_DEMAND"
    node_image         = "projects/clusterdirector-public-images/global/images/family/common-ubuntu-2204-amd64-nvidia-580-slurm-2505-v20251113"
    startup_script     = "#!/bin/bash\necho hello"
    enable_public_ips  = true
    filestores         = [google_filestore_instance.data.id]

    labels = {
      pool = "login"
    }

    boot_disk {
      boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
    }

    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n2-standard-4"
    }

    scaling_spec {
      min_node_count = 1
      max_node_count = 1
    }
  }

  node_pools {
    id                 = "respool"
    zone               = "us-central1-b"
    provisioning_model = "RESERVATION"
    node_image         = "projects/clusterdirector-public-images/global/images/family/common-ubuntu-2204-amd64-nvidia-580-slurm-2505-v20251113"
    startup_script     = "#!/bin/bash\necho hello"
    enable_public_ips  = true
    filestores         = [google_filestore_instance.data.id]

    labels = {
      pool = "respool"
    }

    boot_disk {
      boot_disk_size_gb = 100
      boot_disk_type    = "pd-ssd"
    }

    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n2-standard-4"
      reservation_affinity {
        reservation_affinity_type = "SPECIFIC_RESERVATION"
        values                    = [google_compute_reservation.res.id]
      }
    }

    scaling_spec {
      min_node_count = 0
      max_node_count = 1
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `node_pools` -
  (Required)
  The spec of the pools of different resources.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_node_pools).

* `orchestrator_spec` -
  (Required)
  The spec of the orchestrator. Only one orchestrator may be specified.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_orchestrator_spec).

* `model_development_cluster_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the cluster, which is the final component
  of the ModelDevelopmentCluster's resource name.
  This value should be 1-10 characters, and valid characters
  are `/^[a-z]([a-z0-9-]{0,8}[a-z0-9])?$/`. When using `slurm_spec`,
  hyphens are not allowed (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,9}$/`).


* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The display name of the ModelDevelopmentCluster.
  The name can be up to 128 characters long and can consist of any UTF-8
  characters.

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The labels with user-defined metadata to organize PersistentResource.
  Label keys and values can be no longer than 64 characters
  (Unicode codepoints), can only contain lowercase letters, numeric
  characters, underscores and dashes. International characters are allowed.
  See https://goo.gl/xmQnxf for more information and examples of labels.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `lustre_export_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for backing up the Managed Lustre instances attached to a
  cluster to a Cloud Storage bucket.
  By default every instance attached to any node pool is backed up; set
  `lustres` to narrow that to a subset. Each instance is written to its own
  prefix under the bucket, so several instances, and several clusters, can
  share a destination.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_lustre_export_config).

* `network` -
  (Optional)
  Network spec of the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_network).

* `runtime_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The runtime spec of the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_runtime_spec).

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region of the ModelDevelopmentCluster. eg us-central1

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_node_pools"></a>The `node_pools` block supports:

* `boot_disk` -
  (Optional)
  Represents the spec of disk options.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_node_pools_boot_disk).

* `effective_flex_start_max_duration` -
  (Output)
  The effective maximum duration for instances in this node pool.
  This field reflects the value of `flex_start_max_duration` if it is
  set by the user, or the server-applied default (for example, 7 days) if it
  is not.
  This field is only applicable when `provisioning_model` is set to
  `FLEX_START`.

* `enable_public_ips` -
  (Optional)
  Whether to enable public IPs for the node pool.

* `filestores` -
  (Optional)
  List of the existing Filestore instances to be mounted.
  For example:
  if "projects/my-project/locations/us-central1-a/instances/my-instance" is
  specified, the instance will be mounted to the node pool under the path
  "mnt/filestore/"

* `flex_start_max_duration` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum duration for instances in this node pool.
  This field is only applicable when `provisioning_model` is set to
  `FLEX_START`.

* `id` -
  (Required)
  The unique ID referring to this node pool.

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The labels with user-defined metadata to organize the node pool. These
  labels are applied to the underlying compute resources (for example, the
  VM instances) of the node pool, so they appear in billing exports and
  Cloud Monitoring filters.
  Label keys and values can be no longer than 64 characters
  (Unicode codepoints), can only contain lowercase letters, numeric
  characters, underscores and dashes. International characters are allowed.
  See https://goo.gl/xmQnxf for more information and examples of labels.

* `lustres` -
  (Optional)
  List of the existing Google Managed Lustre instances to be mounted.
  Similar to the filestores, the instance will be mounted to the node pool
  under the path "/mnt/lustre/"

* `machine_spec` -
  (Required)
  Specification of a single machine.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_node_pools_machine_spec).

* `node_image` -
  (Optional)
  The node image to be used for the VMs in the node pool.
  In format of "projects//global/images/" or
  "projects/test-project/global/images/family/"

* `provisioning_model` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the provisioning model for the node pool.
  Behavior for `PROVISIONING_MODEL_UNSPECIFIED`:
  - For CPU node pools: Defaults to `ON_DEMAND`.
  - For GPU node pools:
  - If
  `machine_spec.reservation_affinity`
  is set, it defaults to `RESERVATION`.
  - If
  `machine_spec.reservation_affinity`
  is NOT set, this is an INVALID state and the request will be rejected.
  An explicit `provisioning_model` must be provided.
  ## Constraints:
  `machine_spec.reservation_affinity`
  must not be set if `provisioning_model` is `ON_DEMAND`, `SPOT` or
  ## `FLEX_START`.
  `machine_spec.reservation_affinity`
  must be set if `provisioning_model` is `RESERVATION`.
  Possible values:
  ON_DEMAND
  RESERVATION
  SPOT
  FLEX_START

* `scaling_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The scaling spec of the node pool.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_node_pools_scaling_spec).

* `startup_script` -
  (Optional)
  Startup script for the node pool instances.

* `zone` -
  (Optional)
  The zone of the node pool.


<a name="nested_node_pools_boot_disk"></a>The `boot_disk` block supports:

* `boot_disk_size_gb` -
  (Optional)
  Size in GB of the boot disk (default is 100GB).

* `boot_disk_type` -
  (Optional)
  Type of the boot disk. For non-A3U machines, the default value is
  "pd-ssd", for A3U machines, the default value is "hyperdisk-balanced".
  Valid values: "pd-ssd" (Persistent Disk Solid State Drive),
  "pd-standard" (Persistent Disk Hard Disk Drive) or "hyperdisk-balanced".

<a name="nested_node_pools_machine_spec"></a>The `machine_spec` block supports:

* `machine_type` -
  (Required)
  The type of the machine.
  See the [list of machine types supported for
  prediction](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/configure-compute#machine-types)
  See the [list of machine types supported for custom
  training](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/configure-compute#machine-types).
  For DeployedModel this field is optional, and the default
  value is `n1-standard-2`. For BatchPredictionJob or as part of
  WorkerPoolSpec this field is required.

* `reservation_affinity` -
  (Optional)
  A ReservationAffinity can be used to configure a Vertex AI resource (e.g., a
  DeployedModel) to draw its Compute Engine resources from a Shared
  Reservation, or exclusively from on-demand capacity.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_node_pools_machine_spec_reservation_affinity).


<a name="nested_node_pools_machine_spec_reservation_affinity"></a>The `reservation_affinity` block supports:

* `reservation_affinity_type` -
  (Required)
  Specifies the reservation affinity type.
  Possible values:
  NO_RESERVATION
  ANY_RESERVATION
  SPECIFIC_RESERVATION

* `values` -
  (Optional)
  Corresponds to the label values of a reservation resource. This must be the
  resource name of the reservation, reservation block, or reservation sub-
  block.

<a name="nested_node_pools_scaling_spec"></a>The `scaling_spec` block supports:

* `max_node_count` -
  (Optional)
  maximum size of the node pool,
  must be ≥ min_node_count

* `min_node_count` -
  (Optional)
  minimum size of the node pool,
  must be >= 0 and <= max_node_count

<a name="nested_orchestrator_spec"></a>The `orchestrator_spec` block supports:

* `slurm_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The Slurm orchestrator related spec of the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec).


<a name="nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec"></a>The `slurm_spec` block supports:

* `config` -
  (Optional)
  Cluster-scoped Slurm settings, emitted as global `Key=Value` lines in
  slurm.conf.
  Keys are Slurm parameter names exactly as documented by SchedMD
  (https://slurm.schedmd.com/slurm.conf.html), matched case-insensitively.
  Values are written the way slurm.conf writes them, including composite
  forms such as `bf_window=1440,bf_resolution=600`.
  Example:
  { "PriorityType":            "priority/multifactor",
  "PriorityWeightAge":       "1000",
  "PreemptMode":             "SUSPEND,GANG",
  "SchedulerParameters":     "bf_window=1440,bf_resolution=600" }
  Unsupported, reserved, or misspelled parameters, and values that are not
  legal for the parameter, are rejected at request time with the offending
  parameter named; they are never silently dropped. Settings
  that apply to a single partition or node pool belong in
  `SlurmPartition.config` or `SlurmNodeSet.config` instead -
  several parameters (e.g. `DefMemPerCPU`, `OverTimeLimit`, `PreemptMode`)
  are valid at more than one scope with different meanings and different
  legal values.
  On update this map is replaced wholesale; supply the complete desired set.

* `default_partition_id` -
  (Optional)
  Id of the partition that Slurm jobs submitted without an explicit
  partition run on, for example `sbatch` without `--partition`. Must match
  the `id` of one of `partitions`.
  If unset, the service uses the first entry of `partitions` and this field
  stays empty; the cluster always has a default partition whether or not this
  field is set. Setting it makes the choice independent of list order, which
  matters because `partitions` is replaced wholesale on update: reordering
  the list, or prepending a partition to it, otherwise moves the default and
  silently redirects every job submitted without `--partition`.

* `epilog_bash_scripts` -
  (Optional)
  Custom bash scripts executed after each slurm job on every allocated node.

* `home_directory_storage` -
  (Required)
  Full name of the Filestore to be mounted as /home directory on every node.

* `login_node_pool_id` -
  (Required)
  The node pool id to be used as slurm login node.

* `node_sets` -
  (Optional)
  Node-scoped Slurm settings, keyed by node pool. At most one entry per node
  pool. Node pools without an entry use the settings derived by the cluster's
  Slurm controller.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec_node_sets).

* `partitions` -
  (Optional)
  The Slurm partitions spec.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec_partitions).

* `prolog_bash_scripts` -
  (Optional)
  Custom bash scripts executed before each slurm job on every allocated node.


<a name="nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec_node_sets"></a>The `node_sets` block supports:

* `config` -
  (Optional)
  Node-scoped Slurm settings, emitted as additional `Key=Value` pairs on the
  `NodeName=` line for this node pool's nodes in slurm.conf.
  Example:
  { "Features":     "a3mega,nvlink",
  "Weight":       "10",
  "MemSpecLimit": "4096" }
  On update this map is replaced wholesale; supply the complete desired set.

* `node_pool_id` -
  (Required)
  Id of the node pool these settings apply to. Must match the `id` of one of
  the node pools in the cluster.

<a name="nested_orchestrator_spec_slurm_spec_partitions"></a>The `partitions` block supports:

* `config` -
  (Optional)
  Partition-scoped Slurm settings, emitted as additional `Key=Value` pairs
  on this partition's `PartitionName=` line in slurm.conf.
  Example:
  { "MaxTime":       "4-00:00:00",
  "DenyAccounts":  "low-pri",
  "PriorityTier":  "20",
  "OverSubscribe": "YES:4" }
  Note: values set here take precedence over service-computed defaults for
  the same parameter (for example `OverSubscribe` and `DefMemPerCPU`, which
  the service otherwise derives from the partition's exclusivity and from
  the memory per CPU of its nodes).
  `Default` is rejected here: which partition is the default is a
  cluster-scoped choice, so it belongs in `SlurmSpec.default_partition_id`.

* `id` -
  (Required)
  Id of the slurm partiton

* `node_pool_ids` -
  (Required)
  Node pools for the slurm partition

<a name="nested_lustre_export_config"></a>The `lustre_export_config` block supports:

* `days_of_week` -
  (Optional)
  Days of the week on which a backup runs, each at most once and
  none of them DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED. If empty, a backup runs every day.

* `destination_bucket` -
  (Required)
  The Cloud Storage bucket that backups are written to, without
  the "gs://" scheme.

* `lustres` -
  (Optional)
  The Managed Lustre instances to back up, each named as
  "projects/{project}/locations/{zone}/instances/{instance}". Every entry
  must be attached to one of the cluster's node pools, and no entry may
  repeat. If empty, every attached instance is backed up.

* `start_time` -
  (Optional)
  Represents a time of day. The date and time zone are either not significant
  or are specified elsewhere. An API may choose to allow leap seconds. Related
  types are google.type.Date and `google.protobuf.Timestamp`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_lustre_export_config_start_time).


<a name="nested_lustre_export_config_start_time"></a>The `start_time` block supports:

* `hours` -
  (Optional)
  Hours of a day in 24 hour format. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and
  typically must be less than or equal to 23. An API may choose to allow the
  value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.

* `minutes` -
  (Optional)
  Minutes of an hour. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and less than or
  equal to 59.

<a name="nested_network"></a>The `network` block supports:

* `network` -
  (Required)
  The name of the VPC network where to create the cluster.
  The `default` network is used if not specified.

* `subnetwork` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the subnetwork in the above network to create the cluster.
  If not specified:
  * for auto mode VPC, the subnet in corresponding region is auto-selected;
  * for custom mode VPC, a new subnet will be automatically created.

<a name="nested_runtime_spec"></a>The `runtime_spec` block supports:

* `service_account` -
  (Optional)
  The default service account used by the cluster when running any workloads
  on it. If not specified, the default compute engine service account will be
  used.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/modelDevelopmentClusters/{{model_development_cluster_id}}`

* `cluster_events` -
  The events of the cluster. Displays the 100 most recent events.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cluster_events).

* `cluster_status` -
  The status information of the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cluster_status).

* `create_time` -
  Time when the ModelDevelopmentCluster was created.

* `name` -
  Identifier. Resource name of an ModelDevelopmentCluster.

* `runtime` -
  The runtime backfilled records of the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_runtime).

* `start_time` -
  Time when the ModelDevelopmentCluster for the first time entered the
  `RUNNING` state.

* `update_time` -
  Time when the ModelDevelopmentCluster was most recently updated.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


<a name="nested_cluster_events"></a>The `cluster_events` block contains:

* `event_message` -
  (Output)
  The detailed description of the cluster event.

* `event_time` -
  (Output)
  The occurrence time of the cluster event.

* `event_type` -
  (Output)
  The type of the cluster event.
  Possible values:
  VM_PROLOG_ERROR
  VM_EPILOG_ERROR
  VM_CONTINUOUS_GPU_ERROR
  VM_SCAN_ERROR
  VM_SLURM_POWER_DOWN
  VM_SLURM_DRAIN
  VM_DELETION
  VM_REPORT_AND_REPLACEMENT
  VM_REBOOT

<a name="nested_cluster_status"></a>The `cluster_status` block contains:

* `detail` -
  (Output)
  The detail description of the cluster status.

* `error` -
  (Output)
  The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for
  different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
  used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
  three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.
  You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
  [API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cluster_status_error).

* `nodes_status` -
  (Output)
  The status information of all the nodes in the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cluster_status_nodes_status).

* `state` -
  (Output)
  The realtime state of the cluster.
  Possible values:
  PROVISIONING
  RUNNING
  STOPPING
  ERROR
  UPDATING


<a name="nested_cluster_status_error"></a>The `error` block contains:

* `code` -
  (Output)
  The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.

* `details` -
  (Output)
  A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of
  message types for APIs to use.

* `message` -
  (Output)
  A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any
  user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the
  google.rpc.Status.details field, or localized by the client.

<a name="nested_cluster_status_nodes_status"></a>The `nodes_status` block contains:

* `create_time` -
  (Output)
  The time when the node was created.

* `detail` -
  (Output)
  The detail description of the node status.

* `instance_id` -
  (Output)
  The VM instance ID of the node.

* `instance_name` -
  (Output)
  The name of the Compute Engine instance associated with the node.

* `last_update_time` -
  (Output)
  The time when the node's current state or detail last changed.

* `node_pool_id` -
  (Output)
  The ID of the node pool.

* `node_pool_type` -
  (Output)
  The type of the node pool.
  Possible values:
  NODE_POOL_TYPE_LOGIN
  NODE_POOL_TYPE_COMPUTE

* `node_state` -
  (Output)
  The state of the node.
  Possible values:
  PREPARING
  RUNNING
  ERROR
  UPDATING

* `physical_host` -
  (Output)
  Physical Host Hardware information.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cluster_status_nodes_status_physical_host).


<a name="nested_cluster_status_nodes_status_physical_host"></a>The `physical_host` block contains:

* `block_id` -
  (Output)
  Name of the block.

* `cluster_name` -
  (Output)
  Name of the physical cluster.

* `host_id` -
  (Output)
  Name of the host.

* `subblock_id` -
  (Output)
  Name of the sub-block.

  three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 120 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 120 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 120 minutes.

## Import


ModelDevelopmentCluster can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/modelDevelopmentClusters/{{model_development_cluster_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{model_development_cluster_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{model_development_cluster_id}}`
* `{{model_development_cluster_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import ModelDevelopmentCluster using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    region = "<-optional value->"
    modelDevelopmentClusterId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ModelDevelopmentCluster using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/modelDevelopmentClusters/{{model_development_cluster_id}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ModelDevelopmentCluster can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/modelDevelopmentClusters/{{model_development_cluster_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{model_development_cluster_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default {{region}}/{{model_development_cluster_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_model_development_cluster.default {{model_development_cluster_id}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
